sections.heading: Who We Are
sections.body: Town Crier is operated by Ivo and the Bea Ltd, a UK-registered company. We are the data controller for the personal information you give us. For any data query, write to privacy@towncrierapp.uk.

sections.heading: What We Collect
sections.body: We keep the collection small. We store a unique user ID, the notification preferences you choose, when you created your account, and when you last used it (we use that date to delete accounts nobody uses, see "How Long We Keep It"). If your sign-in shares an email address, we store it so we can send you email alerts and digests. Sign in with Apple lets you hide your email; if you do, we never store your real email address. For each area you want to watch we store a label, either a centre point and radius or a shape you draw, and the filters and alert settings you choose for it, not your exact address. We keep a short-lived history of the alerts we've sent you (new applications and decisions) and which of them you've read. When you save an application we keep a copy of its details, so it stays readable if the council's record changes. If you subscribe or buy lifetime Pro, we store your tier, which Apple product you bought, its App Store transaction IDs, when it expires or when you bought it, and whether you're in a free trial or a billing grace period. We never see your payment details. If you redeem an offer code, we record which code you redeemed and when. On iOS we store a push token and your device type so we can deliver notifications to your device. No law requires you to give us any of this. Some of it is needed to provide the service you sign up for: without an account and at least one watch zone we can't send you alerts, without an email address we can't send email alerts, and without a push token we can't send notifications to your phone. Parts of the app work without an account (see "Rate Limiting and Abuse Prevention").

sections.heading: Why We Collect It
sections.body: We use your data on two lawful bases under UK GDPR. To deliver the service you asked for (Article 6(1)(b), contract): your account, watch zones, preferences, push token, and subscription information. To keep the service reliable and secure (Article 6(1)(f), legitimate interests): authentication, server-side error telemetry, records of whether our emails were delivered, and limiting the rate of unauthenticated requests to prevent abuse (see "Rate Limiting and Abuse Prevention" below). We do not process any data on the basis of consent, we do not make automated decisions with legal effects on you, and we do not send marketing email.

sections.heading: Who Processes Your Data for Us
sections.body: We use Microsoft Azure to host the service. Your account, watch zones, notifications, and email delivery run on Azure services based in the UK (Azure Database for PostgreSQL, Container Apps, Communication Services, Application Insights). Every request the apps and website make to our servers passes through Cloudflare, which protects the service from attacks and abuse. Cloudflare sees your IP address and the content of each request as it passes it on to us. Our website is served from Azure Static Web Apps in the European Union; this serves the site's HTML, CSS, and JavaScript only, and none of your account data is stored there. We use Auth0 (an Okta company) for sign-in; Auth0 stores your email address and credentials in the United Kingdom. We use Apple's Push Notification Service to deliver iOS alerts, and Apple's App Store to handle subscription billing. We use postcodes.io (UK-hosted) to convert postcodes to coordinates. On the web, and in the iOS app before you sign in, your browser or device asks postcodes.io directly, so postcodes.io receives the postcode you typed and your IP address. Once you're signed in on iOS, our servers ask postcodes.io for you and send only the postcode. We use the UK Government's Planning Data service (planning.data.gov.uk) to look up conservation areas, listed buildings, and other planning designations near an application. We only send it coordinates, no personal data. Maps on the web come from OpenStreetMap. Your browser fetches the map tiles directly, so OpenStreetMap receives your IP address and the part of the map you're looking at. Our own servers also fetch OpenStreetMap tiles to make the map image on a public shared-application page, and that request carries no personal data. Maps in the iOS app come from Apple Maps, so Apple receives your device's IP address and the part of the map you're looking at. We use PlanIt (planit.org.uk) as our source of planning data; we only read from them, we do not send them any of your information.

sections.heading: International Transfers
sections.body: Most of your data stays in the United Kingdom. Apple runs its Push Notification Service, App Store, and Apple Maps from Ireland and the United States. Apple transfers data from the UK under Standard Contractual Clauses, and you can ask Apple for a copy at apple.com/legal/privacy/contact. Azure Static Web Apps, which serves our website, is in the European Union, which the UK recognises as providing adequate data protection. Cloudflare is a United States company with data centres around the world, so a request to our servers can be handled outside the UK, usually at the Cloudflare location nearest to you. Cloudflare is certified under the UK Extension to the EU-US Data Privacy Framework, so transfers to it are covered by the UK's data bridge with the United States (the Data Protection (Adequacy) (United States of America) Regulations 2023). If that certification ever lapses, Cloudflare falls back on Standard Contractual Clauses in its Data Processing Addendum, which you can request a copy of by writing to privacy@towncrierapp.uk. Some of our UK-based processors, notably Microsoft Azure and Auth0, are subsidiaries of United States companies. Although your data is stored and processed in the UK, a US parent company could in principle receive a legal demand from US authorities. Both providers publish Data Processing Agreements committing to notify us of, and contest, any such demand where legally permitted. You can request a copy of those agreements by writing to privacy@towncrierapp.uk.

sections.heading: Cookies and Similar Storage
sections.body: We do not set tracking cookies and we do not use third-party analytics. What we keep on your device is there to make the app work, so we do not ask for consent to use it. On the web, your browser's local storage holds your Auth0 sign-in tokens, so you stay signed in, your theme (light or dark), and how you last sorted your list of applications. On iOS, your sign-in tokens are kept in the device keychain. The app also keeps your settings on the device: your theme, your list sort order, the watch zone you last looked at, whether you've finished setting up, and your subscription tier so the app opens quickly. If you use the app before you sign in, it keeps the postcode you searched for and any watch zones you set up on the device, so they're still there when you create an account. It also keeps simple counts of how you use the app, such as how many days you've opened it and how many applications you've saved, so it can pick a sensible moment to ask for an App Store review. Those counts never leave your device.

sections.heading: Rate Limiting and Abuse Prevention
sections.body: When you use the parts of the app that work before you sign in, your requests are not tied to an account. To stop those anonymous requests being abused, for example someone tiling the country with queries to scrape our whole dataset or to overload the free service we read planning data from, we limit how many requests come from each network (IP) address in a short window and slow down any address that sends too many. We rely on our legitimate interest in keeping the service available and secure for this (UK GDPR Article 6(1)(f)). For this we hold your IP address only in memory, for the length of that short window, and discard it as soon as the window passes. We do not write it to our logs, we do not save it to any database, and we never use it to identify you, track you, or build a profile of you. Cloudflare, which sits in front of our servers, also sees your IP address (see "Who Processes Your Data for Us" above). This is the only use we make of IP addresses on our own servers, and it does not change our position that we do not track you.

sections.heading: How Long We Keep It
sections.body: Your notifications and decision alerts are automatically deleted after 90 days. We delete an iOS push token as soon as Apple tells us it's no longer valid, and in any case 180 days after your device last registered it with us. Everything else (your account, watch zones, saved applications, preferences, and subscription status) is kept for as long as your account stays active. If you don't use Town Crier for 12 months, we automatically delete your whole account and everything in it, including your sign-in record, so we don't hold your data for longer than we need to (UK GDPR Article 5(1)(e)). Our server logs and telemetry are deleted after 30 days. They can include your account ID, so we can trace a fault to the account it affected. Email delivery logs, which record the address each email went to and whether it arrived, are also deleted after 30 days. Database backups are kept for 7 days, so anything you delete is gone from our backups within a week. You can also delete your account at any time from the app settings, which removes your profile, preferences, watch zones, notifications, saved applications, and device registrations from our systems.

sections.heading: Your Rights Under UK GDPR
sections.body: You can ask us for a copy of your data (Article 15), correct it (Article 16), delete it (Article 17), receive it in a machine-readable format (Article 20), restrict how we use it (Article 18), or object to how we use it (Article 21). The app provides self-service account deletion and a self-service machine-readable data export covering your profile, preferences, watch zones, notifications, decision alerts, saved applications, device registrations, subscription metadata, and offer code history. To exercise any other right, email privacy@towncrierapp.uk and we will respond within one month. If you're unhappy with how we've handled your data, tell us at privacy@towncrierapp.uk. We'll acknowledge your complaint within 30 days, look into it, keep you updated, and tell you the outcome. You can also complain to the Information Commissioner's Office at any time at ico.org.uk/make-a-complaint or by calling 0303 123 1113.

sections.heading: Security
sections.body: Your data is encrypted in transit with TLS and at rest using Azure's default encryption. Access to our systems uses Auth0 for authentication. We do not log request bodies or passwords.

sections.heading: Children, Changes, and Contact
sections.body: Town Crier is not directed at children under 13 and we do not knowingly collect data from anyone under 13. We may update this policy as the service changes; the "last updated" date at the top of this document shows when we last revised it. For any question about your data or this policy, write to privacy@towncrierapp.uk.
